passage:
Before the new school year, the parent group held a used uniform sale. Families could bring clean uniforms their children had outgrown. Other families could buy them at low prices.
Some students felt shy about wearing used uniforms. But the school explained that many uniforms were still in good condition. Buying them saved money and reduced waste.
At the sale, students helped sort shirts, pants, and jackets by size. They found that most clothes looked almost new.
The sale helped many families. It also changed how students saw second-hand things.
Used does not always mean poor or bad. Sometimes it means practical, careful, and ready for another student's story.
